title: Waste Mining Lab Awarded NSU Research Grant for AI-Powered Campus Bioeconomy
search_description: North South University has awarded competitive research grant funding to Waste Mining Lab to develop and pilot smart dustbin units equipped with computer-vision sorting, converting campus cafeteria food waste into bio-fertilizer.
excerpt: North South University has awarded competitive research grant funding to Waste Mining Lab to develop and pilot smart dustbin units equipped with computer-vision sorting, converting campus cafeteria food waste into bio-fertilizer.
body_html:
Waste Mining Lab has commenced work on an innovative applied sustainability initiative funded by North South University. Led by Dr. Asef Mohammad Redwan as Principal Investigator, the project combines edge artificial intelligence with circular bioeconomy processes.

The research team is engineering smart receptacle stations with real-time optical image classification to automate solid waste segregation at the point of disposal. Collected cafeteria organic waste will be processed through thermophilic digestion and aerobic composting, generating verified bio-fertilizers for campus landscaping and establishing a measurable model for institutional circular bioeconomies.
